evidence.note: Discovered confirm route mis-categorized all non-card errors as payment_intent_unexpected_state and that string errors couldn't distinguish state/missing/card errors; responded with a structural rewrite of store.py to return structured error dicts and propagated the fix across routes — updating the underlying model, not patching one endpoint.

Recognized decline test cards were wrongly rejected at PM creation (402); revised the card-validation model so declines happen at confirm time, correcting a falsified assumption about the Stripe contract.

Further corrected card validation to accept only Stripe test PANs (reject others as invalid_number), refining the contract model after earlier over-permissive behavior — shows iterative evidence-driven adjustment.
Repeatedly identified the idempotency lock-leak as a structural failure mode and reworked release handling rather than ignoring it, treating it as a systemic concern.
Caught payment_intent.succeeded firing on manual capture and revised event emission to only fire on actual success/at capture — a targeted root-cause fix.

reasoning: The agent consistently let contradicting evidence rewrite its design: the structured-error rewrite (31-32) and card-validation model revisions (43, 52) show it treating divergences as signals about the Stripe contract and propagating fixes across related endpoints, matching the level-8 anchor and touching the level-10 'structural pivot' behavior. It stops short of 10 because of visible churn — wholesale rewrites and flip-flopping card logic indicate the initial models were loosely anchored, and corrections came mainly from self-review reasoning rather than fluid, verified-work-preserving evidence loops.
